claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately captures the general rule in 14 CFR § 61.56(a) stating that, except as provided in paragraphs (b) and (f), a flight review consists of a minimum of 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training. The summary, scope, and descriptive modality are fully supported.

Claim C0001 faithfully combines the mandatory components of a flight review specified in 14 CFR § 61.56(a)(1) and (a)(2), requiring both a review of current general operating and flight rules of part 91 and a review of discretionary maneuvers and procedures. Modality, scope, and summary are fully correct.

Claim C0002 faithfully reflects 14 CFR § 61.56(b), allowing glider pilots to substitute a minimum of three instructional flights in a glider, each including a flight to traffic pattern altitude, for the 1 hour of flight training required under paragraph (a).

Claim C0003 correctly states the prohibitive rule of 14 CFR § 61.56(c) prohibiting any person from acting as PIC unless both accomplishing a flight review in a rated aircraft and receiving a logbook endorsement within the preceding 24 calendar months, preserving all governing exceptions.

Claim C0004 accurately states the exemption in 14 CFR § 61.56(d)(1) for individuals who have passed a pilot proficiency check or practical test conducted by an examiner, check airman, or U.S. Armed Force within the 24-calendar-month period.

Claim C0005 accurately reflects the complete set of practical test exemptions for flight instructor actions under 14 CFR § 61.56(d)(2)(i)-(iv), combining all alternatives faithfully with appropriate disjunctive grouping and modal force.

Claim C0006 accurately reproduces the exemption under 14 CFR § 61.56(e) for persons who have satisfactorily accomplished one or more phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program within the 24-calendar-month period.

Claim C0007 accurately reflects 14 CFR § 61.56(f), exempting a flight instructor certificate holder from the 1 hour of ground training if recent experience requirements under § 61.197 or refresher course reinstatement under § 61.199(a)(1) have been met within the 24-calendar-month period.
Claim C0008 correctly captures 14 CFR § 61.56(g) exempting student pilots with training and solo flight endorsements from flight reviews. No inventory unit was defined for paragraph (g).
Claim C0009 accurately captures the permission in 14 CFR § 61.56(h) permitting flight reviews to be combined with § 61.57 requirements. No inventory unit was defined for paragraph (h).

Claim C0010 accurately captures 14 CFR § 61.56(i)(1) regarding the use of flight simulators or flight training devices in approved part 142 training center courses. No inventory unit was defined for paragraph (i)(1).

Claim C0011 accurately captures 14 CFR § 61.56(i)(2) conditioning flight simulator usage on meeting takeoff and landing requirements unless approved for landings. No inventory unit was defined for paragraph (i)(2).

Claim C0012 accurately reflects 14 CFR § 61.56(i)(3) requiring flight simulators or flight training devices to represent an aircraft or set of aircraft for which the pilot is rated. No inventory unit was defined for paragraph (i)(3).

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0000, which faithfully reproduces the rule that a flight review consists of a minimum of 1 hour flight and 1 hour ground training, subject to paragraphs (b) and (f).
Covered by claim C0001, which includes the mandatory review of general operating and flight rules of part 91.
Covered by claim C0001, which includes the mandatory review of maneuvers and procedures necessary for demonstrating safe exercise of pilot privileges.
Covered by claim C0002, which accurately reflects the glider pilot substitution of three instructional flights to traffic pattern altitude for the 1 hour flight training requirement.
Covered by claim C0003, which captures the requirement to accomplish a flight review in a rated aircraft given by an authorized instructor within the 24-calendar-month period prior to acting as PIC.
Covered by claim C0003, which captures the requirement for a logbook endorsement certifying satisfactory completion of the flight review within the 24-calendar-month period prior to acting as PIC.
Covered by claim C0004, which accurately states the exemption for passing a pilot proficiency check or practical test within the preceding 24 calendar months.
Covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the exemption for passing an examiner practical test for issuance of a flight instructor certificate within the 24-calendar-month window.
Covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the exemption for passing an examiner practical test for an additional flight instructor rating within the 24-calendar-month window.
Covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the exemption for passing an examiner practical test to meet recent experience requirements under § 61.197(b)(1) within the 24-calendar-month window.

Covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the exemption for passing an examiner practical test for reinstatement of flight instructor privileges under § 61.199(b)(2) within the 24-calendar-month window.
Covered by claim C0006, which reflects the exemption for satisfactorily completing one or more phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program within the 24-calendar-month period.
Covered by claim C0007, which incorporates the ground training exemption for flight instructors completing recent experience requirements under § 61.197 within the 24-calendar-month period.

Covered by claim C0007, which incorporates the ground training exemption for flight instructors reinstating privileges via an approved flight instructor refresher course under § 61.199(a)(1) within the 24-calendar-month period.
